summary: The Windows GPUI Kit editor saved the second of two identically titled items and displayed the committed title after restart. InlineEdit owns the draft and save state; store::rename_item_if_current checks the stored title and returns the accepted value after commit.
evidence: cargo test --locked --workspace --test desktop_edit: 1 passed. A forced PostgreSQL commit failure left the exact draft in the editor and the previous board intact on reconnect. Retrying the retained draft succeeded. A conflicting rename preserved the draft and allowed reverting to the newer stored title.

cargo test --locked -p rustday-desktop --features native-smoke --test windows_smoke -- --nocapture: 1 passed. In the first window, submitting three spaces with Enter showed rejection and Retry, with the draft and focus retained. Clicking Save on the corrected draft showed Saving… with Save disabled while the row was locked, then Saved with the trimmed title after the lock was released.

The first process closed and exited. A fresh PostgreSQL connection confirmed both original item IDs in order. A second process opened the same board and displayed Review above Review artwork, then closed successfully. The test dispatched keyboard and pointer events to real window controls; it did not check pixels or physical input. Remaining parity gaps are recorded in docs/workflows.md.

cargo test --locked --workspace passed all 6 integration tests. cargo build --locked --workspace --bins, cargo fmt --all -- --check, and cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings passed.
